name: Conrad Washington DC
positioning: Contemporary, art-forward luxury hotel in an all-glass Herzog & de Meuron building at CityCenterDC in downtown Washington
best_for: Travelers who want a modern, design-led base a short walk from the White House
Guests who value club-level service with a dedicated lounge and private chef

facts.text: The hotel is located in downtown DC at CityCenter.
The hotel is a few blocks from the Convention Center and a short walk to the White House.
The building was designed by Herzog & de Meuron.
The building has an all-glass exterior.
The building is LEED Gold Certified.
The lobby, check-in and main dining and lounging spaces are on the third floor.
Interiors firm Rottet Studio designed the rooms with a contemporary decor and a muted palette of whites, grays and light woods.
All rooms have marble bathrooms with double vanities, walk-in showers and Byredo bath amenities.
Suites have extras like low-slung couches and fireplaces.
Estuary, the signature restaurant on the third floor next to the atrium, serves breakfast, lunch and dinner overlooking the Park at CityCenterDC.
Sakura Club Ambassadors personalize the stay of Sakura Club guests.
The gym has walls of windows.

highlights.text: The contemporary art collection, curated by Tatar Art Projects, pays homage to the Washington Color School.
Guests staying in a Sakura Club room or suite have complimentary access to the Sakura Club.
A private Sakura Club chef prepares breakfast and dinner options in the club.
Corner King rooms have a wraparound wall of windows.

considerations.text: Sakura Club access is not available as a Hilton Honors upgrade or as a Diamond member benefit.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting may lack resort-style amenities.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Conrad Washington, DC
